deseq_results <- read.csv("~/Documents/School/thesis/PFAS_project_R-analysis/data/deseq_results/DESeq2_analysis_results-2026-11-06-PFBS-DMSO_pfas-1_10-chemical_duration-all-stat-decreasing/deseq2_results.csv")

```{r}
head(deseq_results)
```

```{r}
ggplot(deseq_results, aes(x = log10(baseMean), -log10(padj))) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 1) +
  # geom_point(na.rm = TRUE) +
  # geom_smooth(method = "gam", color = "red", se = TRUE) + # gam for large datasets >1000
  labs(
    title = "BaseMean Compared to P-value Adjusted",
    x = "baseMean (log10)",
    y = "-log10(padj)"
  ) +
  # geom_hex(bins = 60) +
  # scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent()) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, NA)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_minimal()

```

-log10(padj)
the pvalue is more significant going up the graph (up y axis as y increases)
